children: UBS identified Lockheed Martin
, United Airlines

and eight other companies as its highest-conviction industrial stock picks, arguing that a recovery in manufacturing and broader capital spending could create opportunities beyond the artificial intelligence and data-center boom.
The investment bank’s industrials analysts selected one Buy-rated company from each of 10 coverage areas. The choices also include C.H. Robinson Worldwide
, BorgWarner
, UL Solutions
, Solstice Advanced Materials
, Eaton
, Advanced Drainage Systems
, United Rentals
and Packaging Corp. of America
The price targets imply upside ranging from 21% for Eaton to 62% for Advanced Drainage Systems, based on closing prices from Sept. 11.

For investors, the report presents a case for widening exposure to industrial companies as operating cash flow strengthens and capital investment spreads to manufacturing, transportation, defense and construction. UBS said earnings estimates for many companies exposed to that trend are rising, although higher interest rates and a weaker-than-expected economic cycle remain risks.
Cash flow supports broader capital spending

UBS equity strategists said the industrial backdrop is improving after a manufacturing recession that lasted nearly three years. Inventory reductions are easing, short-cycle indicators are turning higher and capital spending outside AI infrastructure appears poised to accelerate.
Operating cash flow outside the technology sector increased by $436 billion, or 20%, from a year earlier, according to the report. Technology-related cash flow rose by $387 billion, or 37%.

UBS estimated that companies outside the major cloud-computing providers have about $768 billion in additional operating cash flow available for capital expenditures, research, operating expenses and shareholder distributions through next year.
The firm expects non-AI industrial growth to accelerate to about 5% in the third quarter and 6% in the fourth quarter.
Lockheed Martin offers defense growth at discount
Lockheed Martin is UBS’s preferred aerospace and defense electronics stock. Its $674 price target implies 29% upside.

UBS expects rising missile and munitions production, F-35 sustainment work and the CH-53K helicopter program to support several years of growth. Its 2028 revenue and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization estimates are 6% and 13% above consensus, respectively.

The shares trade at about 11.7 times estimated next-12-month ebitda, a discount to defense peers and the broader market. UBS sees room for the valuation to rise as Lockheed converts its backlog into sales, expands margins and generates more free cash flow.
United Airlines could deliver an earnings surprise
UBS assigned United Airlines a $137 price target, representing 25% upside.
The bank believes the market is effectively pricing in 2027 earnings of about $12.20 a share. UBS forecasts $15.21, compared with the consensus estimate of $14.77.

Continued revenue growth, restrained industry capacity and moderating non-fuel expenses could drive earnings growth of more than 60% in 2027, according to the analysts. United trades at roughly seven times UBS’s 2027 earnings estimate, a valuation the firm considers too low given the airline’s premium-cabin and loyalty-program businesses.
Technology could lift C.H. Robinson’s margins
C.H. Robinson carries a $230 price target, implying 51% upside, the second-highest projected return among the 10 selections.

UBS expects technology investments and productivity measures to help the freight broker expand margins in its North American Surface Transportation business, even without a strong recovery in the trucking market.
The bank’s 2027 earnings estimate is 9% above consensus. It forecasts operating margins of 34% in 2026 and 38.2% in 2027 as C.H. Robinson moves toward its 40% target.
BorgWarner looks beyond automobiles
BorgWarner is the analysts’ favorite automotive supplier, with a $95 price target and 43% potential upside.

UBS sees a possible catalyst from a capacity expansion or customer order for the company’s TurboCell microturbine technology. Power generation and other businesses outside the automotive market could contribute about 31% of operating profit by 2030.
The bank’s average EBIT forecasts for 2028 through 2030 are about 15% above Wall Street estimates, reflecting its more optimistic view of BorgWarner’s expansion into non-automotive markets.
UL Solutions may rebound after its selloff
UBS described UL Solutions as a high-quality professional-services company capable of generating sustainable organic growth of 5% to 7%.
The shares had declined about 20% since the company’s second-quarter earnings report, creating what UBS views as an attractive entry point. The bank’s $96 target implies 35% upside.

UBS expects third-quarter organic growth of 5.7%, slightly above the 5.5% consensus estimate. It also projects an ebitda margin of 28.6%, compared with the Street forecast of 28.3%. Higher revenue or margin guidance after the quarter could help revive the stock.
Solstice offers electronics and nuclear exposure
UBS sees about 30% upside in Solstice Advanced Materials, based on its $80 target.

The firm believes the termination of Solstice’s proposed ESI acquisition has created an attractive buying opportunity. It forecasts an ebitda compound annual growth rate of about 10% through 2030, supported by electronics demand, refrigerant regulations and opportunities in nuclear power.
An announcement about expanding nuclear-related production capacity alongside third-quarter earnings could provide an additional catalyst.
Eaton’s earnings power is set to climb
UBS recently upgraded Eaton to Buy and raised its price target to $515, implying 21% upside.
The bank expects organic sales to grow by more than 10% annually during the next three years. Pricing actions and better execution should also improve margins beginning in the third quarter.
UBS projects that Eaton’s earnings power will increase 46% over two years, reaching $19.95 a share in 2028. That estimate is 7% above consensus.
Advanced Drainage Systems has the most upside
Advanced Drainage Systems offers the greatest potential return in the group. UBS’s $207 price target represents 62% upside.

The bank expects increasing use of thermoplastic drainage products and stabilization in construction markets to support volume growth. Its acquisition of NDS also provides revenue and cost-saving opportunities.

UBS believes concerns about resin-cost inflation are excessive because the company has historically managed pricing effectively. The analysts expect adjusted ebitda margins to bottom in fiscal 2027 before expanding by more than half a percentage point annually through fiscal 2030.
The stock trades at about 10 times ebitda, compared with the roughly 15-times multiple used to derive UBS’s target.
United Rentals could benefit from megaprojects
UBS set a $1,350 price target for United Rentals, implying 36% upside.

The bank expects nonresidential construction spending to reaccelerate during the second half of 2026 and into 2027. Semiconductor plants, pharmaceutical facilities, data centers and power projects should stimulate demand for rental equipment.
UBS forecasts rental revenue growth of 12.1% in 2026 and 10.3% in 2027, both above consensus. Adjusted ebitda growth is projected to accelerate from 2.3% in 2025 to 10.6% in 2026 and 9.4% in 2027.
Packaging Corp. could gain pricing power
Packaging Corp. of America rounds out the list with a $292 target and 25% potential upside.

Containerboard producers removed about 10% of industry capacity last year, tightening operating rates. UBS expects Packaging Corp. to realize at least $60 a ton from its proposed September increase of $140 a ton.

That level of pricing could add approximately $345 million to annualized ebitda, though inflation would offset part of the benefit. Two earlier increases, acquisition synergies and a mill reconfiguration provide additional potential upside.

UBS believes stronger pricing signals, reliable execution and the company’s first dividend increase since 2022 could lift its valuation from 9.6 times projected ebitda toward the bank’s target multiple of 11.7 times.

title: UBS names 10 high-conviction industrial stocks as capital spending broadens
